metadata.description: Tests whether iter-4 CAMA failure (d=-1.38) on Amazon item-ltv was due to insufficient training (5 vs 10 epochs) or architectural difference (CAMA vs RAMA). Runs 2 methods x 5 seeds x 10 epochs with per-epoch gate evolution tracking.

test_target_status.reason: RelBench hides test labels for item-ltv

deviations: Removed review_text and summary from review table to prevent OOM: 20.8M rows * 2 cols * 300d = ~50GB
Removed customer_name from customer table to save ~2.2GB

iter2_rama_10epochs.note: RAMA with full rank proxy + cardinality gating

iter4_cama_5epochs.note: CAMA underperformed baseline with only 5 epochs

interpretation.epoch_effect: CAMA gates diverged from 0.5 initialization at epoch 1 over 10 epochs
interpretation.instability_source: Baseline MAE std=0.34. Moderate baseline variance. CAMA trained normally (best epochs: [9, 9, 10, 6, 6]).
interpretation.conclusion: CAMA OUTPERFORMS baseline with 10 epochs (d=13.58, improvement=8.0%). Iter-4 failure (d=-1.38 with 5 epochs) was due to INSUFFICIENT TRAINING TIME, not architectural limitations. With 10 epochs matching iter-2, CAMA achieves an even larger effect size than RAMA (d=13.58 vs d=10.83), suggesting that cardinality-only gating is sufficient and the rank proxy in RAMA is unnecessary.
